title: Hollywood Palace: three years in a vaudeville-style TV show
summary: Under Mitchell Ayres he played acts and rotating hosts on a variety show, unlike a talk-show band.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: How did that differ from what you'd done with Nelson Riddle ?

Well, it was a variety show, like we'd have -- the Russians would send over the movies of an act with a cossack, the horses and all that. So we would have to look at that and put music to it, you know.
It was a variety show, you know.
And then the acts would come over.

Yes, yes, that was a variety show. But they had a different artist every week to emcee the show, like Douglas Fairbanks, Jr. He would emcee the show one week. Bing Crosby, he would emcee the show. Then -- oh, I can't -- just so many people emceed the show. Then he would let me play every now and then, you know. And it was at the old Hollywood Palace show up here, where they had blackouts years ago, the El Capitan Theater, they called it the Hollywood Palace Theater. For three years, I did that. They had a fantastic band. Frank Rosolino was in the band.
Was this sort of the beginning of the -- you know, the kind of thing where -- like Johnny Carson has a band, which you hardly hear at all?

No, this band -- this had no -- like Johnny's a whole show. This was a variety show, like whoever would emcee the show -- we had acts, we had singers, we had -- they had chorus girls. They had a chorus girl for -- about 16 chorus girls and 8 chorus boys.
Oh, it was like a vaudeville show.
Yeah, it was a vaudeville show.
